headline: AFFO climbs, guidance raised despite Fiber-exit GAAP hit
summary_short: Crown Castle's Q2 FY2026 site rental revenue fell 4.1% y/y to $967M and GAAP diluted EPS dropped to $0.22 from $0.67 a year ago, largely reflecting the completed $8.4B sale of its Fiber and Small Cell businesses, while AFFO per share rose 10.8% to $1.13 and full-year AFFO guidance was raised to $1.95B-$2.00B.
summary_long: Continuing-ops income rose 13% y/y to $299M, but GAAP net income fell 68% to $94M as discontinued operations swung to a $205M net loss — the Fiber and Small Cell businesses, sold to EQT and Zayo for $8.4B on May 1, contributed only one month of income plus a $280M disposal loss. Adjusted EBITDA was flat q/q and down 4% y/y to $675M on lower site rental revenue; AFFO rose 9.4% q/q and 10% y/y to $488M on lower interest expense and higher interest income from sale proceeds. Crown Castle repaid over $7B debt and repurchased $1B of stock, ending with $1.25B cash. Management raised full-year AFFO guidance to $1.95B-$2.00B and net income guidance to $730M-$1,010M.

drivers.explanation: Discontinued operations swung to a $205M net loss (from +$26M a year ago): the Fiber/Small Cell businesses only operated through April 30 before the sale closed, plus a $280M loss on disposal was recognized.
Mirrors the net income decline — diluted EPS fell from $0.67 to $0.22 y/y almost entirely because of the discontinued Fiber business swinging to a loss on the completed divestiture.
Decrease was primarily a result of the lower contribution from site rental revenues, partially offset by a decrease in SG&A excluding stock-based compensation expense.
Increase was primarily a result of a decrease in interest expense and an increase in interest income from the use of proceeds from the Fiber and Small Cell sale.
Revenue fell 4.1% y/y as $49M of DISH lease terminations and a $23M drop in straight-lined revenue outweighed 3.9% organic growth from core leasing and escalators.

Management raised full-year AFFO guidance to $1.95B-$2.00B and net income guidance to $730M-$1,010M, citing higher organic site-rental billings and lower opex, partly offset by lower services gross margin.
